linkedin.title: Crude oil distillation process 👇
linkedin.text:
Crude oil distillation process 👇
How Is Crude Oil Transformed into Valuable Products?
Here’s how it works, step by step:
🔹 1. Crude Oil Preheating
Crude oil is heated in a heat exchanger using hot refinery streams.
This improves energy efficiency and reduces fuel consumption.
🔹 2. Desalting
Water, dissolved salts, and suspended impurities are removed.
This helps prevent corrosion, fouling, and equipment damage.
🔹 3. Furnace Heating
Desalted crude oil is heated to approximately 340–370°C.
A mixture of vapour and liquid enters the atmospheric distillation column.
🔹 4. Atmospheric Distillation
Vapours rise through the column while liquids flow downward.
Temperature decreases from the bottom to the top.
Hydrocarbons separate into different fractions based on their boiling ranges.
🔹 5. Product Separation
Refinery gases: LPG and other light hydrocarbons
Naphtha: Gasoline blending and petrochemical feedstock
Kerosene: Jet fuel and other applications
Diesel/gas oil: Diesel fuel and heating applications
Atmospheric residue: Feedstock for further processing
🔹 6. Vacuum Distillation
Atmospheric residue is distilled under reduced pressure.
This allows heavier hydrocarbons to separate at lower temperatures, reducing thermal cracking.
🔹 7. Further Refining
Processes such as catalytic cracking, hydrocracking, and hydrotreating improve product yield and quality.
Final products are blended to meet required specifications.
